description: Rows logged by ground_model report impulse in pound-force seconds while onboard_log uses newton-seconds, so those burns look 4.45 times weaker than they were. Impulse per kilogram of propellant is about 2,160 N·s for onboard_log but about 490 for ground_model; a groupby on reported_by or a scatter of impulse against propellant_g shows two separate lines. This mirrors the real 1999 loss of NASA’s $125M Mars Climate Orbiter, where contractor ground software reported thruster impulse in pound-force seconds instead of newton-seconds; this mission and its log are fictional.
hints: Physics ties some of these columns together. Check whether those relationships hold for every row, and split the rows by each category you have.
Compute impulse per gram of propellant (or per second of burn) and compare it across the two reporting pipelines.
For ground_model rows, impulse per kilogram is about 4.45 times smaller than for onboard_log rows. That is the pound-force-to-newton factor.
